facts.claim: In the Armenian Apostolic marriage service, the right hands of the bride and groom are joined during the exchange of vows, as a sign of the couple's oneness.
facts.conflicts: Parish page of St. Sarkis Armenian Apostolic Church (US parish), not the Mother See; read live 2026-11-03.

facts.claim: The priest blesses the rings, which the bride and groom then exchange.

The rite of crowning is the high point of the Armenian Church wedding service; the crowns stand for the glory and honour with which God crowns the couple, who are crowned as king and queen of their own home.
A cup of wine is blessed in memory of the wedding at Cana, and the couple drink from this common cup as a sign that they will share everything in life, joys and sorrows.
The service closes with a benediction in which the priest asks Christ to protect the couple under the shadow of His cross.
facts.conflicts: The priest's blessing under the cross is sourced; the kavor physically holding a cross over the couple is NOT stated on this page.

facts.claim: One Armenian Apostolic parish's rules (St. Sarkis, US): the sacrament must follow the canons of the Armenian Apostolic Church and may not be held outside the church; a partner from a Protestant denomination must be confirmed in the Armenian Church; the best man must be a member of the Armenian Church; the couple must complete the pastor's pre-marital preparation.
facts.conflicts: Parish-level rules; the Diocese of Australia and New Zealand's rules were not found online in this run. Present as 'for example, one parish asks...' or as a booking-checklist item.

facts.claim: Holy Matrimony in the Armenian Church is described as the sacrament by which two baptised Christians enter a lifelong union by making vows before God and the Church.
facts.conflicts: Parish page of St. James Armenian Church, Watertown MA (US).

facts.claim: One Armenian parish (St. James, Watertown, US) does not hold weddings on Sunday mornings, during Great Lent or Holy Week, or on five major feasts: Armenian Christmas, Easter, the Transfiguration, the Assumption of the Holy Mother of God and the Exaltation of the Holy Cross.
facts.conflicts: Parish rule; Australian diocese calendar not checked. Treat as 'ask your parish priest' guidance.

facts.claim: The same parish asks couples to contact it at least eight months before the wedding and to confirm the priest and church before booking anything else, with at least one pre-marital meeting with the pastor.
facts.conflicts: US parish lead time; not a general rule.

insider_details.detail: Book the parish before anything else: one Armenian Apostolic parish asks for at least eight months' notice and wants the priest and church confirmed before any other wedding booking, so lock the church date first and build the reception and travel around it.

Check the church calendar before choosing a date: at least one parish will not marry couples during Great Lent, Holy Week, on Sunday mornings or on five major feast days, so a spring date near Easter needs the priest's sign-off before guests book flights.

Plan the church running sheet around the crowning, the high point of the service, and the shared cup straight after it; brief the photographer to capture both from below the altar steps, as parishes can restrict where photographers stand.

If one partner is not Armenian Apostolic, raise it with the parish priest early: one parish requires a Protestant partner to be confirmed in the Armenian Church and the best man (the church sponsor) to be a church member, and pre-marital preparation with the pastor is expected.
